title: SYSK Selects: How Capgras Syndrome Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode on Capgras syndrome (often spelled Cotard-style "Capgras" in transcript as "cop Craw"/"cap Cross"), a delusional misidentification disorder in which the sufferer believes close family members or others have been replaced by identical impostors. Hosts cover the statistics, how it differs from prosopagnosia, the skin-conductance studies, the Ramachandran and Hirstein explanation involving disconnected emotional memory and right-brain checking, Freudian and organic explanations, the case of DS, violence associated with the disorder, lack of treatment, and related conditions (Fregoli syndrome, Cotard syndrome, intermetamorphosis, reduplicative paramnesia). The episode closes with a listener mail about sealing in the Mormon church (Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints) and sign-off.

segments.title: Rerun intro and Capgras overview
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Selects episode and the hosts describe Capgras syndrome as a delusion that loved ones have been replaced by impostors, noting the difficulty for both sufferer and the misidentified person.

segments.title: History and prevalence
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the first description of the condition by Capgras and Reboul, the case of Madame M who believed she had many identical husbands, and prevalence estimates among psychiatric patients and Alzheimer's patients.

segments.title: Prosopagnosia contrast and emotional recognition
segments.summary: The hosts contrast Capgras with prosopagnosia (face blindness), explaining skin conductance studies showing emotional responses to familiar faces are missing in Capgras patients.

segments.title: Ramachandran's explanation
segments.summary: The hosts describe Ramachandran's theory that disconnected emotional memory combined with damage to right-brain checking lets the left brain invent an impostor explanation, and mention animals and objects also being affected.

segments.title: Historical and organic explanations
segments.summary: Freudian psychodynamic explanations are described and dismissed, and the hosts discuss organic brain causes, co-occurrence with schizophrenia, epilepsy, bipolar and Alzheimer's, and the file-based memory model.

segments.title: Case of DS and violence
segments.summary: The hosts recount the case of DS, a man who after a car accident believed impostors had replaced people around him, and describe violent incidents linked to the delusion.

segments.title: Treatment and related conditions
segments.summary: The hosts say there is no standard treatment or cure and sometimes medication for an underlying disorder helps. They then cover Fregoli syndrome, Cotard syndrome, intermetamorphosis, and reduplicative paramnesia.

segments.title: Closing and search tips
segments.summary: The hosts reflect on the brain research and suggest search terms, then move to a message break.

segments.title: Listener mail on Mormon sealing
segments.summary: A former Mormon listener explains that men can be sealed to multiple women in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and the hosts note a future episode request on the church.
